question.text: Under Indian tax law, carry forward of speculative losses is allowed for:

answer.text: 4 assessment years from the year of loss

explanation.text: The Logic: Under Indian income-tax rules, speculative business losses are subject to a tighter carry-forward regime than ordinary business losses. The conventional position is that unabsorbed speculative losses can be carried forward for four assessment years immediately following the assessment year in which the loss was incurred, and can only be set off against future speculative profits during that period. The Trap: The 8-year carry forward applies to non-speculative business losses, not to speculative losses. Speculative loss carry-forward is neither indefinite nor disallowed altogether — it is permitted but for a limited window. Note: The specific four-assessment-year carry-forward for speculative losses was not located in the cited Series XVI pages (p.126; p.181-p.182; p.187-p.189; p.94); the workbook's tax section focuses on CTT, GST, stamp duty, and SEBI turnover fees rather than income-tax loss set-off rules.
